primitives.name: Gunslinger Score
primitives.verbatim_quote: Quarterbacks in the upper right are just really good, while those in the lower left are just not very good at anything.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'tds': 'dimensionless count of touchdowns', 'passYards': 'meters', 'rushYards': 'meters', 'shortOfSticksOnThirdRate': 'dimensionless ratio', 'meanAirYards': 'meters', 'alpha, beta, gamma, delta, epsilon': 'dimensionless weights'}
primitives.assumptions: Linear additive weighting of performance components; normalized via z-score scaling; independent variables assumed orthogonal.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( \text{shortOfSticksOnThirdRate} \to 1 \) or \( \text{meanAirYards} \to 0 \), score approaches extremal values indicating high-risk behavior.

primitives.name: Game Manager Score
primitives.verbatim_quote: A game manager doesn't throw interceptions, doesn't take sacks, doesn't take negative plays (which we'll measure by success rate), and complete a lot of passes.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'ints': 'dimensionless count of interceptions', 'successRate': 'dimensionless ratio', 'sacks': 'dimensionless ratio', 'completionPercent': 'dimensionless percentage', 'lambda, mu, nu, omega': 'dimensionless weights'}
primitives.assumptions: Inverse relationship between turnovers/sacks and performance quality; linear combination of stability indicators.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( \text{ints} \to \infty \) or \( \text{sacks} \to \infty \), score tends toward negative infinity.

layer2.mapping: Encodes quarterback consistency and error minimization in a single scalar for predictive modeling in GSE's tactical decision engine.
layer2.telemetry: Z-scored ManageScore per QB-year, used in clustering algorithms to identify stable performers.

primitives.name: Quarterback Archetype Classification
primitives.verbatim_quote: Looking at this graph, quarterbacks in the upper left are true "gunslingers" - high performance as gunslingers, and low performance as game managers.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\tau_G': 'threshold scalar for GunslingScore', '\\tau_M': 'threshold scalar for ManageScore'}
primitives.assumptions: Binary classification based on two-dimensional Euclidean distance from origin in (GunslingScore, ManageScore) space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If both scores exceed thresholds, ambiguous classification; if both below, neutral archetype.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic mapping between empirical performance vectors and abstract archetype manifolds in GSI's latent space.
layer2.telemetry: Classification accuracy across seasons validated via cross-validation of z-scored performance features.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core duality emerges from contrasting quarterback roles: one that prioritizes high variance, high reward (gunslinger) versus one that emphasizes low variance, consistent execution (game manager). These are modeled as projections onto orthogonal subspaces defined by weighted combinations of key statistics—touchdowns, yards, sacks, completions, etc.—standardized via z-scores to ensure comparability across time and teams. The failure mode occurs when these metrics become collinear or misaligned with actual game impact, such as when a quarterback throws many deep passes but fails to convert them into positive EPA. The dual nature implies a phase-space trajectory where a QB may shift between archetypes depending on game state, which is captured through dynamic scoring functions rather than static classifications. This allows for temporal evolution tracking in GSE’s state-transition models.
